scope: Mac Kindle cloned-voice startup latency investigation; no app or backend implementation changes
evidenceLimit: Precise phase timings below are from today's retained Debug logs, not a trace of the user's latest Release click. Release omits those log writers. Do not treat the minimized preparation sample as a normal foreground benchmark.

sample1540.condition: Restart with stale VM, minimized while preparing, then explicitly paused before response
sample1540.interpretation: Two VM constructions are confirmed by source and logs. Exact attribution of the roughly 5.5-second intervals to resume matching, other initialization, or scheduling still needs scoped timing.

sourceFindings: Kindle continuous input bypasses ClonedTTSStartup short-opening splitting and passes a complete bounded unit; English short-opening target elsewhere is 120 UTF-16 units.
Clone API waits for a complete JSON response containing base64 audio; the first segment cannot play while that same response is still being synthesized.
ensureLiveDocument(force:true) rebuilds Read/Explain VMs, then buildKindleSentenceStream rebuilds them again for speech units.

Read VM initialization and metadata configuration can both restore position; Kindle relocation includes bounded OCR context correction. This is a candidate hotspot, not yet a measured cause of the 5.5-second intervals.

Safari source commit 40aada8 uses /api/captioned_speech_partly; Mac uses /api/voice-clone/captioned-speech. Verified production routes both clone requests into handleCaptionedCloneRequest and the same captioned worker.

The unified partly endpoint additionally partitions input (English at most 74 words / 900 upstream characters; other languages first natural sentence). Endpoint spelling alone does not establish a different or faster engine.

Production credits-v1 clone flow includes auth, voice lookup, credit reservation, optional voice preparation, worker synthesis/timestamps, validation, and awaited credit settlement before JSON response.
Worker queue/run response headers are forwarded by the backend but omitted from current Mac timing logs. Successful Vercel requests have no detailed stage timings in the queried logs.

releaseSpotCheck.cachedResume: Play click at 16:12:07 local time returned a Playing AX state in the same approximately 1.3-second tool call; this is UI observation, not an audio first-byte benchmark.
releaseSpotCheck.freshPage: Preparing state observed after Play at 16:15:08; later Playing observed; sparse observations cannot produce an exact startup duration.
releaseSpotCheck.profilingLimit: Release sample began about 14.7 seconds after the fresh-page Play; it does not cover the full preparation interval.

nextPriorities: Instrument and remove redundant pre-TTS document/VM preparation while preserving verified reading-position recovery.
Use a shorter first complete speech unit with source mapping preserved, then retain enough read-ahead for fast playback and page transitions.
Record worker queue/run and backend phase timings with request correlation and no source text or credentials; compare same text, voice, cache state and route against extension.
